name: MA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 11-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Auchincloss's incumbency and huge financial advantage ($7.3M cash vs. $1.3K)
Republican challenger is minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Auchincloss: an 11-point Democratic district, incumbency, and a fundraising gap of roughly 140-to-1, with no outside spending against him. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, and no polls or ratings suggest any reason to move off the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Auchincloss or an unusually strong Republican environment in Massachusetts could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jake Auchincloss seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by 11 points, in a year when the national environment also favors his party. He enters the general election with a large war chest, about $7.3 million on hand, after raising over $3.6 million, and faces no outside opposition spending.

Republican Thomas Stalcup has raised only about $26,000 and reports roughly $1,300 in cash, with no measurable outside support, leaving him little capacity to communicate with voters. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 97 percent. With no public polling of the race, the forecast rests on district lean, incumbency, and the stark resource gap, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
